title: API Request and Response Models knowledge check

questions.prompt: What should a robust asynchronous API wrapper do?
options: Treat a declared response type as a server-side authorization check.
Model success and failure, check response status, and validate decoded data before treating it as a domain object.
Trust response.json() because its result is automatically verified by TypeScript.
questions.answer_key: Model success and failure, check response status, and validate decoded data before treating it as a domain object.
questions.explanation: The type checker does not validate remote data; asynchronous operations can fail independently.

questions.prompt: Which statement is correct about “API Request and Response Models”?
options: The learner should publish hidden solutions so the exercise can grade itself.
The concept should be demonstrated with request body types and checked against its intended contract.
The safest approach is to skip diagnostics and trust the first output.
A type assertion automatically validates every value at runtime.
questions.answer_key: The concept should be demonstrated with request body types and checked against its intended contract.
questions.explanation: The supplied syllabus explicitly includes “Request body types”; connect it to a concrete example and verify the behavior relevant to this lesson.

questions.prompt: What is a good verification step after practicing “API Request and Response Models”?
options: Check response shapes, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
Assume optional and versioned fields is unnecessary because the code has type annotations.
Ignore compiler or test failures if the interface looks correct.
Treat passing a static token check as proof that the program executed correctly.
questions.answer_key: Check response shapes, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.explanation: The syllabus includes “Response shapes”. Verification should match the concept: type-level checks, runtime tests, configuration checks or human review as appropriate.
